{{Short description|Swiss mathematician}}

'''Laurent Bartholdi''' is a Swiss mathematician working in the areas of [[geometric group theory]], [[symbolic dynamics]], and [[computational complexity]]. He is particularly well-known for his contributions to the study of [[Grigorchuk group|self-similar groups]] and [[Amenable group|amenability of groups]]. Currently Bartholdi is a
[[CNRS|CNRS Directeur de Recherche]] at Institut Camille Jordan, [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]]<ref>[https://math.univ-lyon1.fr/icj/recrutements/ Recrutements, 2025], Institut Camille Jordan, [[Claude Bernard University Lyon 1]]. Accessed 22 July 2025</ref> in France.

Bartholdi received a PhD in Mathematics in 2000 from the [[University of Geneva]], with [[Pierre de la Harpe]] and [[Rostislav Grigorchuk]] as co-advisors.<ref>[https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46526 Laurent Bartholdi], [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]. Accessed 7 June 2025.</ref>

In June 2025 Bartholdi delivered the inaugural [[Paul Schupp]] Distinguished Lecture at the GAGTA 2025 "Groups, Logic and Computation" conference at the [[Stevens Institute of Technology]].<ref>[https://web.stevens.edu/algebraic/Stevens2025/index.htm  Groups, Logic and Computation: Interactions between geometric group theory, model theory and computer science], [[Stevens Institute of Technology]]. Accessed June 9, 2025.</ref>
